output.name: Telvar

anatomy.part: top apex of the kite, the head
bottom corner of the kite, where the tail is tied
the lamp, hung at the centre of the kite
the knot in the tail-string where it bends
the small lantern at the end of the tail

output.myth: When Aun cut the string and the sky drifted off over the water, the boats out on the Upper Sea lost their way in the dark. Those on the rocks could see nothing but black. So Ennu, who sews the cloth for every kite, made one that carries a small oil lamp up the line on still nights. Hesk winds it slow, one turn for every hand's breadth, so it will not snatch. Tavo came down the cliff one night and tore at the cloth, laughing, and the lamp swung wild, but the cord held. Its light fell on the water, and the boats coming in from the Leeward dark saw the harbour and turned. Sil saw it too from her drowned place, and was glad, though she did not say so. Mend your kites before the weather comes, child. A lamp on a string is the nearest thing to flying back that anyone has managed.
output.verse:
A lamp on the line
Ennu sewed; Hesk wound it slow
so boats find the shore
